[![nf-test](https://github.com/YiannisGal/ont16s/actions/workflows/nf-test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/YiannisGal/ont16s/actions/workflows/nf-test.yml) [![nf-core linting](https://github.com/YiannisGal/ont16s/actions/workflows/linting.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/YiannisGal/ont16s/actions/workflows/linting.yml) [![Nextflow](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-%E2%89%A525.10.4-green?style=flat&logo=nextflow&logoColor=white&color=%230DC09D&link=https%3A%2F%2Fnextflow.io)](https://www.nextflow.io/) [![run with docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/run%20with-docker-0db7ed?labelColor=000000&logo=docker)](https://www.docker.com/) [![nf-core template version](https://img.shields.io/badge/nf--core_template-4.1.0-green?style=flat&logo=nfcore&logoColor=white&color=%2324B064&link=https%3A%2F%2Fnf-co.re)](https://github.com/nf-core/tools/releases/tag/4.1.0) ## Introduction **ont16s** is a Nextflow pipeline for **full-length 16S rRNA gene amplicons sequenced on Oxford Nanopore** (e.g. SQK-16S114, SQK-MAB114). It turns raw reads (BAM or FASTQ) into taxonomic abundance tables with [Emu](https://github.com/treangenlab/emu), and checks the data and the result along the way: - **any samples**: environmental, host-associated or mock communities, from one to hundreds; - **any Emu database**, with its provenance recorded (Emu's default database, SILVA 138.2 grouped by genus, or your own); - **automatic pooling** of shallow samples, so that rare taxa are not lost to Emu's per-run abundance floor; - **quality checks with reasons**: duplicated reads, reads lost in filtering, low depth, unassigned reads, organelles, database fit; - **mock-community validation** against expected composition (presence/absence and proportions). It is built on the [nf-core](https://nf-co.re) template (tested modules, pinned containers, CI). ## Pipeline overview ```mermaid flowchart LR A[BAM / FASTQ
samplesheet] --> B[Merge chunks
BAM → FASTQ] B --> C[NanoPlot
raw] B --> D[chopper
length / quality filter] D --> E[seqkit rmdup
remove duplicate reads] E --> F[NanoPlot
filtered] E --> G{Emu mode
auto} G -- per sample --> H[Emu per sample] G -- pooled --> I[Emu on all samples
split per sample] H --> J[Post-processing
exclusion, metrics] I --> J J --> K[Combined tables] J --> L[Mock validation] E --> M[Database fit] J --> N[Run summary
and warnings] C & F & L & N --> O[MultiQC report] ``` 1. **Read preparation**: merge chunks of the same sample, convert unaligned BAM to FASTQ ([samtools](https://www.htslib.org/)), concatenate/compress FASTQ. 2. **Read QC** before and after filtering ([NanoPlot](https://github.com/wdecoster/NanoPlot)). 3. **Length/quality filter** ([chopper](https://github.com/wdecoster/chopper); default 1,000–2,000 bp). 4. **Duplicate-read removal** ([seqkit](https://bioinf.shenwei.me/seqkit/)): identical reads written twice (e.g. overlapping chunks) are removed and reported. 5. **Taxonomic profiling** with [Emu](https://github.com/treangenlab/emu), per sample or pooled across samples (`--emu_mode auto` decides). 6. **Post-processing**: optional taxon exclusion (e.g. chloroplasts), per-sample read accounting. 7. **Outputs**: per-sample and combined tables (species and genus, abundance and counts), database provenance, mock validation, run summary and warnings, [MultiQC](https://multiqc.info/) report. ## Quick start Requirements: [Nextflow](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/install.html) ≥ 25.10.4 (Java 17+) and [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/). ```bash # 1. Run the built-in test (downloads a 0.7 MB test BAM and a 1.5 MB test database) nextflow run YiannisGal/ont16s -r main -profile test,docker --outdir results_test ``` The test takes about 2–3 minutes on 2 CPUs and should report the 12 expected bacteria of a Zymo mock community (`results_test/mock_validation/mock_validation_summary.tsv`). ```bash # 2. Run your data nextflow run YiannisGal/ont16s -r main \ -profile docker \ --input samplesheet.csv \ --emu_db /path/to/emu_db \ --outdir results ``` ## Installation 1. **Nextflow** (≥ 25.10.4, needs Java 17 or newer): ```bash curl -s https://get.nextflow.io | bash mv nextflow ~/bin/ # or any directory on your PATH nextflow -version ``` 2. **A container engine.** Docker is the tested option (`-profile docker`). Profiles for `singularity`, `apptainer`, `podman` and `conda` are provided by the nf-core template but have not yet been tested with this pipeline. 3. **The pipeline.** Nextflow downloads it on first use (`nextflow run YiannisGal/ont16s -r main`). While the repository is private, either clone it and run the local copy: ```bash git clone git@github.com:YiannisGal/ont16s.git nextflow run ./ont16s -profile test,docker --outdir results_test ``` or give Nextflow a GitHub token (`export NXF_SCM_FILE` / `~/.nextflow/scm`, see the [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/git.html)). 4. **An Emu database** (see [Databases](#databases)). Use `-r ` (e.g. `-r 0.1.0`) to run a fixed release. ## Test data `-profile test` uses public data from [YiannisGal/ont16s-test-datasets](https://github.com/YiannisGal/ont16s-test-datasets): | File | Content | | ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `zymo_msplus/zymo_msplus_mab114_sup_rep1_sub1pct.bam` | 546 reads (1 % subset) of an ONT Zymo mock (R10.4.1, SUP, SQK-MAB114-24), ONT Open Data, CC BY-NC 4.0 | | `emu_db_zymo_genera.tar.gz` | Emu default database reduced to the 15 genera of the mock (955 species) | How they were made (commands, checksums, licences) is documented in that repository. ## Samplesheet One row per reads file; files with the same `sample` are merged. ```csv sample,reads,mock soil_rep1,/data/soil_rep1.fastq.gz, zymo_ctrl,/data/run1/FBB32095_pass_0.bam,zymo_msplus zymo_ctrl,/data/run1/FBB32095_pass_1.bam,zymo_msplus ``` | Column | Required | Description | | -------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `sample` | yes | sample name, no spaces | | `reads` | yes | unaligned BAM, `.fastq`, `.fq`, `.fastq.gz` or `.fq.gz` (path or URL) | | `mock` | no | name of a mock community definition (e.g. `zymo_msplus`, `zymo_d6306`, `zymo_d6331`); empty for real samples | ## Databases `--emu_db` takes a directory with `species_taxid.fasta` and `taxonomy.tsv`, or a `.tar`/`.tar.gz` archive of it (local path or URL). | Database | Best for | How to get it | | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Emu default (rrnDB v5.6 + NCBI 16S RefSeq, 2020) | species-level names in well-studied communities (mocks, host-associated) | `osf -p 56uf7 fetch osfstorage/emu-prebuilt/emu.tar` | | **SILVA 138.2 grouped by genus** | environmental samples with many uncultured lineages; labels organelles | build from Emu's SILVA download with [`bin/build_silva_genus_db.py`](bin/build_silva_genus_db.py) (see [usage](docs/usage.md#choosing-a-database)) | | your own | anything else | any Emu-format database | The checksums and size of the database used are written to `pipeline_info/emu_db_provenance.tsv` in every run. ## Main parameters | Parameter | Default | Description | | ----------------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `--input` | — | samplesheet (CSV) | | `--outdir` | — | output directory | | `--emu_db` | — | Emu database (directory or archive) | | `--emu_mode` | `auto` | `per_sample`, `pooled`, or `auto` (pooled when ≥ 25 % of samples have < 10,000 filtered reads) | | `--min_read_length` / `--max_read_length` | 1000 / 2000 | read length window (bp) | | `--min_read_qual` | 0 (off) | minimum mean read quality | | `--emu_type` | `map-ont` | minimap2 preset used by Emu | | `--exclude_taxa` | — | comma-separated lineage terms to remove, e.g. `chloroplast,mitochondria` | | `--mock_definitions` | `assets/mocks` | directory of mock definitions | All parameters, thresholds and their justification: [docs/usage.md](docs/usage.md), or `nextflow run YiannisGal/ont16s --help`. ## Outputs | Directory | Content | | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `emu/` | per-sample Emu tables; `emu-combined-{species,genus}[-counts].tsv` (taxa × samples); `pooled/` in pooled mode | | `ont16s_report/` | `ont16s_run_summary.tsv` (one row per sample) and `ont16s_warnings.tsv` (every warning with its reason) | | `mock_validation/` | per-mock-sample expected vs observed taxa and a summary (recall, false positives, L1 distance) | | `qc/` | NanoPlot reports (raw/filtered), Emu read accounting, database fit | | `multiqc/` | MultiQC report combining QC, warnings and validation | | `pipeline_info/` | software versions, database provenance, Nextflow reports | Details: [docs/output.md](docs/output.md). ## Validation Measured with this pipeline (details and data in [docs/server-tasks](docs/server-tasks/)): | Dataset | Result | | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Zymo MSPlus mock, ONT R10.4.1 SUP (ST-001, ST-008) | all 12 expected bacteria detected; 0.6 % of abundance assigned to unexpected taxa | | Environmental samples, PRJNA925180 (soil, lake, freshwater; ST-004) | replicates agree (Bray-Curtis ≤ 0.27), habitats separate (0.62–0.92) | | Lake-sediment core, 70 samples, R10.4.1 fast basecalling (ST-005–009) | vs a published NanoCLUST + SILVA analysis of the same reads: same between-sample pattern (Mantel r = 0.96 phylum, 0.95 genus), all published phyla detected, 36 min on 24 CPUs; [comparison](docs/etoliko-method-comparison.md) | Not yet done: an independent-laboratory mock (NaMeco, PRJEB82315), tests on HPC/cloud, and proportion accuracy against Zymo's expected 16S composition. ## Limitations - Taxonomy depends on the database; Emu assigns every read to its closest reference, so organisms absent from the database appear under a related name. - No representative sequences are produced (yet). - Tested on Linux x86_64 with Docker; other container engines and ARM64 are not yet tested. ## Credits ont16s was written by IGaliatsatos ([@YiannisGal](https://github.com/YiannisGal)). ## Citations If you use ont16s, please cite the tools it runs, listed with references in [CITATIONS.md](CITATIONS.md), in particular: > Curry KD, Wang Q, Nute MG, et al. Emu: species-level microbial community profiling of full-length > 16S rRNA Oxford Nanopore sequencing data. _Nat Methods_ 19, 845–853 (2022). > doi: [10.1038/s41592-022-01520-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-022-01520-4) and the database you used.
